system.name: SONiC DASH SmartSwitch
system.one_liner: a uni-box hardware model that converges an NPU and multiple DPUs in a top-of-rack switch to offload cloud network services at scale

content.key_idea: SONiC DASH SmartSwitch collapses Sirius's separate rack, servers and switches into one uni-box device that slots into a compute row's existing T1 position, stacking an SDN controller, SONiC, and NPU+DPU hardware behind the DASH-SAI API.

summary: This paper offloads cloud network services onto SONiC DASH SmartSwitch, a uni-box hardware model that converges an NPU and multiple DPUs, replacing the prior DPU-centric Sirius appliance. Figure 1 argues the case in two panels. Panel (a) shows a datacenter elevation view: Sirius needs its own purpose-built rack with extra servers and ToR-equivalent switches (blocked from ad hoc placement among compute rows), whereas a SmartSwitch (SST1) simply takes the place of a compute row's existing T1 switch. Panel (b) gives the logical architecture: Sirius disaggregates network processing onto a separate pool of DPU-equipped servers reached through several switch-hierarchy hops (T3/T2/MoR-T1/ToR-T0), while SONiC DASH SmartSwitch collapses this into one box, stacking an SDN controller running a DASH pipeline, SONiC (gNMI/Redis/switch-state) invoking a DASH-SAI API, and the SmartSwitch hardware itself, where an NPU forwards packets to multiple DPUs (each with an ASIC and a CPU running DPAPP) over an interconnect, with community/hardware-provider contribution points marked alongside.
summary_zh: 该图对比Sirius与SmartSwitch部署：前者需独立机架和额外服务器交换机，后者可直接替代机架内T1交换机；逻辑上前者经多级交换连至DPU服务器池，后者将控制器、SONiC与NPU/DPU整合为一体。
notes: Panel (b) actually contains two sub-diagrams (a Sirius topology sketch and a detailed SmartSwitch stack); the component list covers the named boxes in both. Some very small repeated icons (individual rack units, VM circles) are omitted from the component list for brevity.
